title: Grab and Move - Force Z-Order to Top
author: rdefeofds

status.label: Duplicate request
status.detail: Open issue #47647 already tracks raising a window to the foreground when Grab and Move interacts with it.

next_action.label: Post duplicate response
next_action.reason: Consolidate the z-order option and multi-monitor scenario under #47647.

judgment.rationale: The requested behavior—raise the touched/moved window above other windows—is the same optional foreground behavior requested in open issue #47647.
evidence: The current issue asks to force the moved window to the top so it cannot slide under windows on another monitor.
#47647 asks Grab and Move to raise the touched window in front of others and discusses an optional setting.
A commenter on the current issue already linked #47647 as the existing request.
Current GrabAndMove movement calls SetWindowPos with SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE, deliberately preserving z-order and activation.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a duplicate response linking #47647 and close this parallel request.

issue_context.summary: Moving a window with Grab and Move can leave it behind windows on the destination monitor; the reporter wants an option to raise it during interaction.
known_information: The requested behavior is either always-on or configurable.
The desired result is compared with Win+Shift+Arrow, where the moved window remains available.
Open issue #47647 requests the same bring-to-foreground behavior.
GrabAndMove currently moves and resizes with SWP_NOZORDER and SWP_NOACTIVATE.
inferences: Changing z-order may interact with focus-stealing rules and Always On Top semantics, but those design questions belong in the existing canonical request.
issue_context.analysis: The linked issue is not merely similar; it asks for the same optional raise-on-interaction behavior. Current source confirms z-order preservation is explicit, so consolidating the product decision is preferable to parallel design.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue, its single comment, labels, and timeline.
Read the body and all eight comments of #47647 and confirmed it remains open.
Inspected GrabAndMove/main.cpp movement and resize calls, which pass SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE.

actions.label: Post duplicate response

comment.body: Thanks for describing the multi-monitor z-order case. This is already tracked in #47647, which requests the same Grab and Move option to raise the touched window in front of other windows. The current implementation deliberately moves/resizes with z-order and activation unchanged, so the focus/foreground product decision should stay in that existing thread. Please continue the scenario on #47647 and close this issue as a duplicate.
